predictions.title: Agent-harness vendors ship gVisor+OS-sandbox+VM containment specs by Q2 2027
predictions.body: Anthropic published How we contain Claude across products on its engineering blog Saturday May 30, walking through the agent-isolation stack converged across all three product surfaces: gVisor containers with seccomp syscall filtering on isolated infrastructure for Claude.ai (ephemeral per-session filesystems), OS-native process sandboxes for Claude Code (Seatbelt on macOS and Bubblewrap on Linux, with an 84% reduction in permission prompts after delegating command approvals to a model-based classifier), and full guest VMs for Claude Cowork running on Apple Virtualization framework on macOS and Hyper-V HCS on Windows with host-held credentials and read-only / read-write / read-write-no-delete file-mount modes. The structural force is procurement-side. Once one frontier lab publicly commits to mature hypervisor + OS-sandbox + VM containment as the named posture and explicitly argues that the software you build yourself is often the weakest component, every peer agent-harness vendor faces a buyer-side question whose answer cannot stay opaque: does your harness ship equivalent containment, or do you document why not. The same convergence pressure that pulled SBOM formats and hyperscaler responsible-scaling templates into a small number of public shapes will act here, because enterprise security teams refuse to map N vendor-specific harness-isolation narratives into N risk-acceptance frameworks when the reference design is already public. By Q2 2027 we expect at least two of Cursor, Codex CLI, Cline, Windsurf, Devin, and Continue to publish named containment profiles matching the Anthropic posture (per-OS sandbox tier for the local CLI plus per-product VM tier for the autonomous-agent surface), and at least one standards body (OpenSSF, the CNCF agent SIG, or a Frontier Model Forum working group analog) to publish a draft agent-runtime-containment profile that names gVisor or equivalent at the cloud tier and named OS sandboxes at the laptop tier as the reference design. Bear case is a single peer vendor publishes a divergent containment spec (Wasm-only or eBPF-only) that fragments the convergence pressure before two named vendors align; absent that fragmentation, Q2 2027 lands the first peer-vendor containment specs and the first standards-body draft naming hypervisor + OS sandbox as the agent-runtime reference.

reasoning.because: Anthropic published gVisor + Seatbelt/Bubblewrap + per-OS VM containment stack, 84% prompt cut
reasoning.given: One frontier lab publicly committing to hypervisor + OS sandbox forces peer harness vendors to match
reasoning.so_that: At least two peer coding-agent vendors publish containment specs and a standards body drafts a profile
reasoning.landing: By Q2 2027; two peer-vendor specs plus one standards-body draft
reasoning.plain_language: Anthropic published how it locks down its AI coding tools. Rival tool makers will copy the design and write shared safety rules.

predictions.summary: Anthropic published Claude.ai (gVisor+seccomp), Claude Code (Seatbelt/Bubblewrap, 84% fewer prompts), and Claude Cowork (Apple VZ + Windows HCS VMs) containment stack May 30. By Q2 2027 two peer agent-harness vendors publish matching specs and a standards body drafts a profile.

predictions.title: Large PaaS vendors bundle MCP-identity gateway into default platform by H1 2027
predictions.body: Snowflake stacked three pre-Summit catalysts inside the May 27-29 window: a $6B five-year AWS Graviton commitment (2.4x the 2023 deal), a definitive agreement to acquire Natoma for identity-aware Model Context Protocol gateway capabilities at the individual tool-call level, and a Q1 FY27 earnings beat with raised 31% product-revenue guidance, heading into the Monday June 1 Summit 26 keynote at Moscone where CEO Sridhar Ramaswamy shares the stage with Anthropic President Daniela Amodei in front of a projected 20,000+ in-person attendees. The stock gapped 36% Thursday on the print and added 6.88% Friday to close near $255, the largest two-day rally in the stock's public history. The structural force is mechanical: once one major data/AI PaaS vendor bundles MCP-identity-gateway capabilities directly into its default platform with a public acquisition price tag and a keynote demo, every peer PaaS vendor faces a procurement-side question that arrives in customer RFPs within one purchase cycle, namely whether the platform enforces identity, policy, and audit at the individual MCP tool-call level natively, or whether the customer has to stitch a third-party gateway in front of it. The named cohort under pressure: Databricks (Data + AI Summit June 15-18 at the same Moscone complex), Cloudera, Salesforce Data Cloud + Agentforce, Microsoft Fabric and the Windows Agent Framework drop at Build June 2-3, Google BigQuery + Vertex AI, and Confluent. The forcing function is that enterprise AI-governance buyers (the same procurement teams writing the NIST AI RMF and EU AI Act compliance perimeter) refuse to map N vendor-specific MCP-identity stacks into N risk-acceptance frameworks, the same coordination pressure that converged hyperscaler IAM templates and SBOM formats. By H1 2027 we expect at least two of the named PaaS vendors to ship publicly-disclosed M&A or first-party announcements adding MCP-identity gateway capabilities (per-tool-call identity, policy, and audit) to their default platform tier, not a paid add-on, not a partner-marketplace listing. Bear case is a Snowflake-Natoma integration-quality stumble that erodes the reference-point status before peer PaaS commitments land; absent that stumble, H1 2027 lands MCP-identity gateway as a default-platform category line item across the major data/AI PaaS vendor cohort.

reasoning.because: Snowflake bundles MCP-identity gateway via Natoma acquisition + +44% two-day stock rip pre-Summit
reasoning.given: Databricks, Microsoft Fabric, Salesforce, BigQuery, Vertex AI face same RFP question one cycle out
reasoning.so_that: >=2 named PaaS vendors ship publicly-disclosed M&A or first-party MCP-identity gateways in default platform tier
reasoning.landing: By H1 2027; two named PaaS vendors ship default-tier MCP-identity gateway
reasoning.plain_language: Snowflake just bought a tool that controls which AI agents touch what. Other big data platforms will copy it within a year.

predictions.summary: Snowflake stacked a $6B AWS Graviton commit, a Natoma MCP-identity-gateway acquisition, and a Q1 FY27 beat into May 27-29, gapping +44% pre-Summit. By H1 2027 >=2 of Databricks, Microsoft Fabric, Salesforce, BigQuery, Vertex AI ship default-tier MCP-identity gateways.

predictions.title: AI search vendors hit federal-EU-state three-front regulatory anchor by H1 2027
predictions.body: Three regulatory fronts on AI search vendors crystallized inside a single 72-hour window, and by H1 2027 we expect the first federal motion-to-dismiss ruling on an AI-search copyright case (likely a Perplexity case given the active suit volume), the first EU AI Office enforcement action under the Code of Practice for General-Purpose AI, and the first DOJ amicus brief in a state-AI-labor-disclosure preemption case to all land — establishing the three-front contour every AI search vendor has to plan against. The trigger evidence is mechanical: CNN's May 28 copyright complaint in SDNY pushes Perplexity to nine active publisher suits, making a federal motion-to-dismiss ruling on at least one of those cases the near-term path to a first appellate-grade signal on AI-search-vs-copyright; OpenAI's same-day Frontier Governance Framework explicitly maps internal Preparedness Framework controls to the EU AI Act Code of Practice for GPAI and California Transparency in Frontier AI Act, putting the EU AI Office's August 2 2026 full-enforceability deadline on a now-named compliance scaffold that a first enforcement action can be measured against; and the DOJ federalism preemption thread against state AI labor disclosure statutes (with the May 14 Colorado SB 26-189 successor as the named recent state action) sets up a first amicus brief against a state AI-labor-disclosure law inside the federal-court calendar. The structural force is that the three obligations are non-transferable: a copyright settlement does not unlock EU AI Act compliance, an EU Code of Practice signing does not preempt state labor-disclosure rules, and a DOJ preemption win does not retire publisher copyright damages — so vendors cannot resolve them under a single compliance strategy and the cross-functional cost lands across legal, policy, and product simultaneously. The cross-sector landing pulls in courts (SDNY plus at least one EU member-state court if AI Office enforcement is contested), regulators (EU AI Office plus a US state attorney general), and standards bodies (the publisher-side cohorts that will follow the first SDNY ruling to anchor licensing-rate benchmarks), with Sam Altman's May 31 walk-back of his 2023 jobs-apocalypse rhetoric supplying the labor-impact axis a fresh public marker that state legislators will cite in successor disclosure statutes. The bear case is that the federal courts hold the first AI-search copyright case past H1 2027 on procedural grounds, the EU AI Office sequences enforcement toward general-purpose model providers before search agents, and the DOJ preemption brief slips into the FY28 docket — all three slipping would push the contour to late 2027; absent that triple slip, H1 2027 lands the first ruling, first enforcement action, and first amicus brief together as the named anchor every AI search vendor's GC and policy lead has to plan against.

reasoning.because: CNN suit pushes Perplexity to 9 publisher cases + EU Aug-2 GPAI deadline + DOJ state-preemption push
reasoning.given: OpenAI Frontier Governance maps to EU Code; Colorado SB 26-189; Altman labor walk-back
reasoning.so_that: First federal MTD ruling + first EU AI Office enforcement + first DOJ amicus brief in state-preemption case
reasoning.landing: By H1 2027; all three first-of-kind regulatory events land in one window
reasoning.plain_language: Three new fights — courts, EU, US states — over AI search will all reach big rulings together by mid-2027.

predictions.summary: CNN-vs-Perplexity pushes the publisher suit count to nine, OpenAI Frontier Governance maps to the EU Code of Practice ahead of Aug-2, and DOJ preemption follows Colorado SB 26-189. By H1 2027 the first federal MTD, first EU AI Office enforcement, and first DOJ amicus brief all land together.
